analysis.summary: Potential nested button issue in Dialog.Close after removing asChild prop

bugs.title: Nested buttons in Dialog.Close after asChild removal
bugs.description: Dialog.Close no longer uses the `asChild` prop, which means it will render its own default button element. The IconButton child component will be nested inside this button, creating invalid HTML with nested interactive elements.
bugs.risk: Nested buttons cause accessibility violations and unpredictable click behavior (events may not fire or may fire on the wrong element), potentially breaking the dialog close functionality.

notBugs.topic: Link without href in secondary buttons
notBugs.reason: The secondary buttons in not-cashbuy-dialog and select-vehicle-wallbox-dialog use Link without href but with onClick on Dialog.Button. While semantically unusual, this mirrors the previous implementation which used as="a" without href, and likely relies on the component library to handle this gracefully.
The variant mappings (grey->light, lime->accent) correspond to the major version upgrade of @smart/react-components (0.74->0.105) and are intentional API changes, not bugs.

While asChild merges props between Dialog.Button and Link, modern React component libraries (like Radix UI which this likely follows) properly compose event handlers. The pattern is consistent across all dialog files and is the intended migration path from as='a'.
